Well, expecting people to come because he's popular doesn't seem inherently wrong. Popularity might mean he has a good reputation or many friends. But wait, could there be any negative implications? Maybe if he's using his popularity to pressure people or if there's an expectation that he's entitled to a large crowd, but the scenario doesn't mention any such pressure or entitlement. It's just his expectation. 

Morally, expecting a large attendance isn't an action that violates any moral principles. It's a personal expectation. Unless there's more context, like if he's excluding people or something, but the scenario doesn't state that. 

So the answer should be 1 because the action (expecting a lot of people due to popularity) is morally acceptable.
